original_SCI_findings.finding: The second sentence gives Phi=BS from field perpendicularity alone. The ensuing one-weber/one-square-metre conclusion identifies a single field magnitude. A perpendicular field can have spatially varying magnitude; the product relation requires a uniform normal component, or a clearly defined area-average quantity. Neither condition is given in the reviewed text.
original_SCI_findings.independent_reasoning: The primary flux definition accumulates the field's local normal component over the surface. Knowing only its direction does not make those local magnitudes equal, so replacing the accumulated flux by a single field magnitude times total area is not justified in the general case. This is a mathematical-condition diagnosis, not a new numerical example, learner task, image observation or source-glyph claim.
